charts.title: Number of new registrations for health foods with function claims in Japan from fiscal year 2015 to 2023
charts.short: Number of new foods with function claims registrations in Japan FY 2015-2023
charts.description: In fiscal year 2023, more than 1.4 thousand registrations of health foods with function claims were handed in at the Consumer Affairs Agency in Japan. New registrations quadrupled compared to fiscal year 2015, when the "foods with function claims" label was introduced. Functional foods are labeled with claims based on scientific evidence for the effectiveness of the ingredients under the manufacturers' and distributors' own responsibilities.
charts.note: Japan; fiscal years 2015 to 2023; the Japanese fiscal year starts on April 1 of each stated year and ends on March 31 of the following year

charts.title: Awareness of meal substitute products in Japan as of March 2024
charts.short: Awareness of meal replacement products in Japan 2024
charts.description: Around two in three Japanese consumers were aware of meal substitute products, according to a survey in March 2024. The largest share of respondents, 43 percent, stated that they knew what kind of products meal replacements were without having tried them before. Almost 20 percent tried the food supplement products.
charts.note: Japan; March 12 to 13, 2024; 1,018 respondents; 16-69 years

charts.title: Preferred purchase channels for dietary and health supplements in Japan as of February 2024
charts.short: Purchase channels for dietary and health supplements Japan 2024
charts.description: Drugstores were the preferred purchase channels for dietary and health supplements in Japan. As revealed in a survey conducted in February 2024, almost 21 percent of respondents stated that they bought dietary supplements in physical drugstores, with online platforms like Amazon, Rakuten, and Yahoo Shopping following behind.
charts.note: Japan; February 14 to 19, 2024; 3,000 respondents; 20-79 years

charts.title: Leading nutrients consumed as dietary supplements in Japan as of September 2023

charts.description: Lactobacillus were the most consumed nutrient in dietary supplements in Japan, according to a survey conducted in September 2023. charts.title: Distribution of alternative eating preferences in Japan as of January 2023, by diet form
charts.short: Alternative eating habits share in Japan 2023, by diet
charts.description: Low sugar was the most common alternative diet among consumers in Japan, as revealed in a survey conducted in January 2023. The survey revealed further that 4.5 percent of respondents were vegetarians, while only 2.4 percent claimed to be vegan.
charts.note: Japan; January 2023; 2,418 respondents; 20 years and older

charts.title: Most popular aspects of dietary education advice to follow in Japan as of November 2023
charts.short: Dietary advice to follow in Japan 2023
charts.description: A nutritionally balanced diet was the most popular dietary advice consumers in Japan wanted to take up, as revealed in a survey conducted in November 2023. Another popular resolution concerning dietary education was keeping a health-conscious diet, named by 57.1 percent of respondents.
charts.note: Japan; November 1 to 27, 2023; 2,309 respondents; 20 years and older; postal and online survey; multiple answers allowed
charts.source: Central Research Services; MAFF Share of respondents

charts.title: Frequency of balanced meals in Japan as of November 2023
charts.short: Frequency of balanced meals in Japan 2023
charts.description: Over 38 percent of consumers in Japan ate balanced meals almost every day, as revealed in a survey conducted in November 2023. On the contrary, around 13.6 percent of respondents stated they rarely had two meals composed of a grain product, a protein-based main dish, and a vegetable-based side dish in a day. In its 'Fourth Basic Plan on Promoting Dietary Education', the government targets to increase the percentage of people having balanced meals daily to at least 50 percent by 2025.
charts.note: Japan; November 1 to 27, 2023; 2,309 respondents; 20 years and older; postal and online survey; only one answer allowed
